# Code families

> Generated reference for Acta code families and the payload-format registry.
> Every persisted code is documented here exactly once; the data-model reference [`data-model.md`](./data-model.md) links into this file from every code-bearing column.

This release: **29 families**, **152 values**.

> Numeric IDs are stable family-local persistence identifiers. Enum members carry programmatic meaning; textual codes carry operator-facing meaning.
> Numeric grouping is a readability convention, not a runtime schema. Canonical failure states use `200`.
> Unknown values and `255` are rejected in closed families. `JobPayloadFormat` is the explicit exception permitting consumer-defined value `255`.
> Assigned, deprecated, retired, and permanently reserved identities are never reused.

## Human-readable ordering

The numbers are arranged so a raw value gives you a quick hint about the state you are looking at:

- `0` means nothing is selected, enabled, or present.
- Values below `100` represent work that is still active or waiting.
- `100` represents normal successful completion.
- Values between `150` and `199` represent controlled completion, such as rescheduling, suppression, or administrative closure.
- `200` represents failure, exhaustion, or death.
- `220` represents cancellation.
- `230` represents interruption or an unknown outcome.
- `240` represents retirement or deprecation.
- `255` is reserved and rejected in closed code families.

This pattern makes raw values easier to scan in database rows, logs, and diagnostics. Treat it as a visual guide only. Application code must check explicit enum members and must not infer behavior from numeric comparisons.

`JobPayloadFormat` is the one exception: consumer-defined formats may use IDs from `128` through `255`.

| 53 | `job.handler-cancelled` | Handler called ctx.CancelAsync; the attempt was finalized as a deliberate terminal Cancelled (no retry, budget untouched). | Active |
| 54 | `job.handler-paused` | Handler called ctx.PauseAsync; the Job was held in Paused until an external resume (budget untouched). | Active |
| 60 | `job.signal-released` | RaiseSignalAsync set a matching signal and moved a Suspended Job to Ready. | Active |
| 61 | `job.step-retry-scheduled` | An inline step failed within budget (or on replay still awaits its retry instant); the parent re-armed budget-neutral until the step's next_retry_at_utc. | Active |
| 62 | `job.exclusive-key-held` | A claimed exclusive-key job found its key lock held at execution admission; re-armed Ready after the fixed bounce delay (budget-neutral). | Active |
| 63 | `job.step-interrupted` | An at-most-once step was re-entered on replay before its outcome was recorded (worker died mid-flight); the body is not re-run and the parent lands terminal Failed. Non-retryable; the outcome is unknown and must be reconciled externally. | Active |
| 100 | `worker.clean-shutdown` | Worker process exited cleanly via SIGTERM / IHostedService.StopAsync. | Active |
| 101 | `worker.heartbeat-stale` | Worker heartbeat exceeded the liveness window; the sys.recovery system job flipped Status to Dead. | Active |
